children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Tuesday.
WHEAT - Down 5 to 8 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat futures
fell on profit-taking in the overnight trade, market analysts said.

The Kremlin said on Tuesday that there had been further diplomatic contacts about a proposal by Turkey for the safe passage of grain via the Black Sea, and that Russia was finding alternate routes for its grain exports in the meantime.

Russia's Arctic port of Murmansk will use equipment typically used to load fertiliser when it ships its first grain from southern Russia for export as early as next month, as the Black Sea route remains closed due to Ukrainian drone attacks.
Ukraine has harvested 33 million metric tons of grain from 7 million hectares, or from 61% of the sown area, as of September 22, the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday.
Heavy rains will dominate much of Ukraine for at least the next seven days, significantly slowing the harvest of late grains and oilseeds, analysts at farmers' union UAC said on Tuesday.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was 7-1/2 cents lower to $7.19-1/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 11-1/4 cents to $7.83-1/4 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 8-1/4 cents at $7.38 a bushel.
CORN - Down 2 to 5 cents per bushel
CBOT corn
turned lower on profit-taking after Monday's rally in the grain and soybean markets, market analysts said.
Traders are keeping a close eye on weakness in the US dollar and oil markets, as prospects for increased oil supplies from the Gulf eased market concerns.
Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States eases military pressure and lifts its blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday.
Steady rainfall continues across parts of the central US, with harvest in parts of Nebraska and Iowa essentially grinding to a halt for now, two market analysts said.

U.S. corn ratings held steady at three-year lows over the past week, as harvesting of both crops advanced modestly across other parts of the Midwest despite the rains, according to a weekly U.S. Department of Agriculture report released on Monday.

In Europe, the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war forced Russian companies to repurpose fertiliser, coal, and other cargo terminals at Russia's Baltic and Arctic ports to handle grain exports after Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted shipments through the Black Sea, five sources said.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last 4 cents lower at $5.39 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 6 to 7 cents per bushel
CBOT soybean futures

turned lower on Tuesday, as traders hoped that an upcoming meeting between the presidents of the US and China, the world's largest soybean-importing nation, would result in greater demand from the Asian country.

Soybean harvesting was slowed in some areas of the Midwest last week by excessive rains, analysts said, and soggy field conditions and more showers this week are likely to continue restricting harvest progress.

China's state stockpiler Sinograin on Tuesday announced its second large-scale auction of imported soybeans in September, just days ahead of a summit in Washington between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Sinograin also sold 62.4% of the 543,000 tons of imported soybeans offered at an auction on Tuesday, consultancy Mysteel said, marking its first large-scale sale since late August.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last 5-3/4 cents lower at $13.22-1/4 per bushel.
